Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test `testSingleChildOption` indicates a problem with option group constraints not respecting the presence of child groups. The current bug report clarifies that when a Group A is a child of Group B, Group B's minimum or maximum constraints don't consider whether Group A is present because Groups themselves are not added to the CommandLine option set. 

Inspection of the `WriteableCommandLineImpl.addOption(Option)` method shows that when an Option is added, it is recorded in internal data structures (`options` set and `nameToOption` map), but there is no logic to propagate the presence of a Group option to its parent groups. There is even a commented placeholder suggesting to "ensure that all parent options are also added" which currently does not happen.

The `hasOption(Option)` method simply checks if the Option is present in the `options` set. Since Groups are not themselves added when any of their children are present, `hasOption(Group)` returns false even if some child in the Group is present, leading to incorrect enforcement of minimum and maximum constraints on parent Groups.

This matches the bug report's description precisely: the core issue is that `WriteableCommandLine#addOption(Option)` must be modified to recursively add Groups to the CommandLine when any child option inside those Groups is present, so that `hasOption()` can correctly detect their presence. Without this, constraints on Groups fail to behave as expected, causing the test failure.

Recent bug reports are less relevant here since they focus on different failures or test coverage requests; the current report and code inspection provide a clear explanation.

This diagnosis explains why the test detecting group-child interactions fails and points directly to the incomplete logic in `WriteableCommandLineImpl.addOption(Option)` as the cause.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
